lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Pluto's sake, Aeacus, give me the full tour of the underworld.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Not easy, Menippus, the whole thing. But the highlights: that's Cerberus over there, the ferryman who rowed you across, and you've already seen the lake and Pyriphlegethon coming in.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: I know those, and you, gatekeeper that you are. Saw the king too, and the Furies. Show me the old-timers, though — especially the famous ones.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: That's Agamemnon. This is Achilles. Idomeneus next to him. Odysseus. Then Ajax, Diomedes, and the rest of the Greek elite.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Homer, your epic heroes are a sorry sight — just dust and nonsense now, all those famous heads. Truly feeble. Aeacus, who's this one?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Cyrus. That's Croesus. Above him, Sardanapalus. Above them, Midas. And that's Xerxes.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: So this is the one Greece used to shudder at — the bridge over the Hellespont, the man who wanted to sail through mountains. And Croesus looks every bit the part. Aeacus, let me smack Sardanapalus on the head.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Don't. You'll shatter his skull — it's womanish.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Fine. I'll just spit on the hermaphrodite, then.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Want to see the philosophers too?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: By Zeus, yes.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: This first one is Pythagoras.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Greetings, Euphorbus, or Apollo, or whatever name you're using today.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: And to you, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No more golden thigh?

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: Not anymore. But let me check your bag — anything edible in there?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Beans, my friend. Which I assume are still off-limits.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: Just hand them over. Different rules down here. I've learned that beans and the heads of one's parents aren't the same thing anymore.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: This is Solon, son of Execestides. That's Thales. Next to them, Pittacus and the rest. All seven, as you can see.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: These are the only ones who look like they aren't in pain. Cheerful, even. Now, who's the one covered in ash like a burnt loaf, covered in blisters?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Empedocles. Half-cooked from Etna.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: My good man with the bronze shoes, what on earth possessed you to throw yourself into the crater?

lines.speaker: Empedocles
lines.text: Melancholy, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No, it was vanity and pretension and a whole lot of nonsense. That's what charred you, sandals and all — and not undeserved. The trick didn't work, though. You were caught dead. Aeacus, where's Socrates?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Over there with Nestor and Palamedes, still talking.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: I'd still like to see him, if he's around.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: The bald one?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: They're all bald. That doesn't narrow it down.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: The snub-nosed one, then.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Same problem. They're all snub-nosed.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: Looking for me, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Very much so, Socrates.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: How are things in Athens?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Plenty of young men claiming to philosophize. If you saw their postures and the way they walk, you'd think they were the very best.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: I've seen plenty like that.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And you've seen the kind that came to you: Aristippus reeking of perfume, and Plato himself, the one who learned how to flatter Sicilian tyrants.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: What do they say about me?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You're a lucky man, Socrates. They all think you were wonderful, that you knew everything. And — I have to tell the truth — that you knew nothing at all.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: I told them that myself. They thought it was irony.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Who's this crowd around you?

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: Charmides, Phaedrus, and the son of Clinias.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well done, Socrates. Even here you're still chasing the beautiful boys.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: What else would I do? Sit with us, if you like.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No, I'm off to sit with Croesus and Sardanapalus. At least there I'll get some laughs listening to them complain.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: I'm off too, before some dead soul tries to slip past. You'll see the rest later, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Go ahead. This is plenty for now, Aeacus.
